sentence: The concentration in Engineering equips students with a solid foundation for careers in engineering, to advance the knowledge base for future technologies, and to merge teaching, scholarship, and practice in the pursuit of solutions to human needs.

In accordance with Brown University guidelines, Concurrent or Dual enrollment in credit bearing courses and/or degree programs at another postsecondary institution while enrolled as a Brown University degree candidate is prohibited except in cases of established cross registration agreements and/or approved joint degree programs such as the Rhode Island School of Design (in both The College and Graduate School); Wheaton College (The College); Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences (Graduate School only): and IE Business School (Graduate School only).

Students with outstanding performance on these tests, or on the Advanced Placement Tests of the College Entrance Examination Board, may be admitted to advanced courses without the usual course prerequisites.
Brown participates in the Advanced Placement (AP) Program of the College Entrance Examination Board.

Students who report their eligible scores by the designated deadlines will be notified of their eligibility for such placement notations upon matriculation at Brown before their first semester and asked whether they wish to accept or decline transcript notation(s) of advanced placement credit (when indicated by department policy for a subject).

Advanced Placement notations may not be applied to the minimum 30 course credits needed to earn a Brown degree; placement notations carry a value of 0.0 course credit; in other words, they do not earn actual course credit or an enrollment unit in the way that Brown courses do.

To ensure students have the guidance and support they need to make informed choices, the University assigns each new student two advising partners: an exploratory advisor and a Meiklejohn peer advisor.

The exploratory advisor is a faculty member or administrator who provides a long-term institutional perspective on educational options while generally informing, sometimes encouraging, and occasionally challenging students.
As first-year students transition to the sophomore year, they are encouraged to stay with their exploratory advisor to benefit from the continuity and depth of a two-year advising relationship.

The Curricular Resource Center (CRC) provides advising, facilitation, and reference materials for students wishing to design their own courses (ISPs and GISPs), craft independent concentrations, and explore options for time away from Brown.
Brown students take summer courses to enhance their degree work or maintain progress toward degree completion.
Whether you’re undeclared, pursuing a double major, or exploring new areas of study, resources are available to guide your academic path.
If you’re still exploring your academic path, the Exploratory Studies Center is here to help.
Through personalized advising, courses, and hands-on campus experiences, students can discover their strengths, explore majors and careers, and confidently choose a direction.
Visit the Exploratory Studies Center to learn more.
